‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 Episode 8 Recap: Are Roy And Keeley Back Together?

Published

September 23, 2026
By Sourya Sur Roy
Comments(
0
)
Add Us on Google
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by

Instaread

Yet another installment of the AppleTV sports comedy series Ted Lasso is already nearing its end with the release of season 4 episode 8 this week. After having finally found comfort in her surroundings at the Richmond women’s team, Alice Chilton once again struggles with a certain situation regarding their star striker. Meanwhile, Leslie Higgins stumbles upon another concerning matter with regards to the club’s ownership. Finally, Roy Kent and Keeley Jones head to Chelsea together for the ceremony arranged for Roy, and the two get to spend quality time together in season 4 episode 8.

Spoiler Alert

Why does Alice feel guilty?

Ted Lasso season 4 episode 8 begins with a quick update about the Lady Greyhounds’ performance in the 2nd division of the Women’s Super League, as the team soars way higher than anyone had expected them to. Despite being newcomers to professional football, the Richmond women’s team enjoy a hot streak of form with the help of strong defenders and clinical attackers. At the end of the first 16 games of the season, the team have only lost thrice, drawn 4 times, and won 9 games, which is an impressive stat. They sit 2nd on the table, just 4 points behind the league leaders, Birmingham City, with 6 games left till the end of the season. One of the major reasons for Richmond’s overwhelming success has been their clinical striker, Gemma Jay, who began the season as a novice but has now become a star. Gemma is the leading goalscorer in the league, and with her brilliant performances, she is already expected to become a big name in women’s football in years to come.

But things take a turn during a game between Richmond and Charlton Athletic, with the home side leading through two goals by Gemma. With the scoreline already settled and the coaches confident that they will win it, Ted decides to replace the striker and give someone young a chance. He surely has both Gemma and the young striker in mind when wanting to make this substitution, but Gemma is not happy about it. She clearly states that she wants to continue playing, and so Ted asks his fellow assistant coaches what to do. While Beard does not have too strong an opinion, Alice Chilton suggests that he lets Gemma continue on the pitch so she can try and get a hat-trick. This is definitely a changed version of Alice, who almost went through a therapeutic realization in the last episode and learned how to open up to people. Having practiced all the social skills she had picked up, Alice now genuinely wants to do good to everyone and support them in their personal endeavors. Therefore, she now advices Ted to let Gemma keep playing, so she can get her hat-trick and receive a massive boost to her confidence. However, Gemma sustains an unfortunate but significant injury in the last stage of the game, because of which she has to be substituted anyway. With the injury being severe enough to rule her out for the entire season, Alice eventually starts to blame herself for the whole thing, believing she should not have suggested that Gemma be kept on the pitch. Because of this feeling of guilt, she eventually goes on to have a breakdown in front of Ted, and this is when she once again realizes the healing effect that he can have on everyone around.

Dealing with the situation in his indirect but effective manner, Ted gathers all the players in the dressing room, with both his assistant coaches joining him as well. It was not just Alice who was affected by Gemma’s injury and her resulting absence, as the players were also concerned and dejected, which was evident from their lack of interest in training. Therefore, Ted talks to them about the need to gather courage and support their teammate through their performance, but most importantly, he sneaks in a speech about how crying is very natural in the high-intensity sport of football. The words, spoken to the entire squad, are actually meant for Alice, who finally realizes that she is in a very safe space, where she can open up to anyone at any time, not just in an overwhelmingly positive and sweet way, but also when things are not going her way and she is scared or disappointed. Thus, having once requested to leave Richmond at the very beginning of the season following the appointment of Ted Lasso as the head coach, Alice Chilton now walks up to Rebecca Welton’s office and very openly talks to her about the need to support Gemma, and also the rest of the team, during this difficult time. She then goes on to visit Gemma at her house as well, but more on that later. Towards the end of the episode, it is Alice who gathers everyone at the hospital right before Gemma is about to go in for an MRI scan. From having once struggled to consider herself a part of the team, Alice now unites everyone behind the injured striker and becomes an invaluable member of the squad.

Is Gemma really out for the season?

The initial tests run on Gemma’s injured knee are not very conclusive, as the injury is determined to possibly be a sprained ligament, which will keep her out of action for 6 to 8 weeks. However, there is also a very high possibility that it is much more serious and will require immediate surgery, which will surely keep her out for the rest of the season. The only way to have the intensity of the injury confirmed will be to wait for the swelling in her knee to go down and then have an MRI test done to pinpoint the exact problem. There is also a situation with regards to the head doctor at the team, Dr. Strudwick, who informs Rebecca that he can check on Gemma only by the end of the week, meaning that the striker will have to sit with her injury for a few days. Keeley is understandably upset with the situation, as she questions why Strudwick is so unbothered about the star player from the women’s team, as he would have definitely rushed in to help had a star from the men’s team faced a similar injury. Both because of Keeley, and also encouraged by her new friend, Zelda Southport, Rebecca decides to confront the doctor over a phone call. Although she intends to put some professional pressure on the doctor and ensure that he comes in to check on Gemma at the earliest, he simply takes advantage of the situation to end their arrangement. Dr. Strudwick is rather unhappy at having to work for both the men’s and women’s teams at the club, with no significant increase in his salary, and so when Rebecca threatens to fire him from the men’s team if he doesn’t care about their female counterparts, he decides to cut ties with the club altogether. As a result, a different doctor has to be involved, and as per Keeley’s wish, it is ultimately Erin Beaumont, the ex-girlfriend of Roy Kent, who steps in as the team doctor for the Lady Greyhounds, at least temporarily.

But before the MRI test, there is one more matter to deal with, especially for Alice, as Gemma herself loses interest in pursuing football as a career following her injury. She moves in with her mother and contemplates retiring, especially now that she has been offered an internship role at a very prestigious law firm. Gemma admits to Alice that she knows pursuing law as a career will bring her much more wealth in a shorter time than playing professional football in the 2nd division, and so she genuinely feels like calling it quits. This is one more reason for Alice feeling down throughout the episode, as she feels that Gemma is basically trying to shy away from facing difficult times. Therefore, after she musters up her courage to do so, Alice visits Gemma at her house once again and advises her to rethink the situation. She explains that she will totally support Gemma if she genuinely doesn’t want to play football anymore. But Alice does not want Gemma to feel scared and uncertain because of her injury, which does actually provide the young footballer some perspective. After all, she is extremely talented and easily one of the best strikers in the league already. With all these insights, Gemma ultimately postpones the internship opportunity and feels mentally ready to return to the game. But before that, she needs to undergo the MRI test to see how soon she’ll be ready physically. Ted Lasso season 4 episode 8 ends right as Gemma’s MRI begins, meaning that we don’t know the results yet. What is certain, though, is that she will still be an important member of the team even if she is ruled out for the rest of the season.

Who has been buying the shares from the stakeholders?

While going through the files in his office, the Director of Football Operations at Richmond, Leslie Higgins, comes across a concerning document which he had not paid attention to till now for some reason. As he looks into the matter, Leslie learns that a significant portion of the shareholders in the club have been selling off their shares in recent times. Since Richmond had let the fans buy 49% of the club earlier, Leslie has details of everyone who has sold their shares in the recent times, and he calls them up for more information. Eventually, he has to go around the neighborhood to make direct enquiries as well, before he finally gets some solid information from Mae at her pub. 

Certain things are very clear from the information that Leslie gathers, starting with the fact that many of the fans/stakeholders did not actually want to sell their shares, but had been forced or convinced to do so by someone. Secondly, whoever bought their shares strictly warned them against talking about the sales to anyone, which is why Leslie faces a lot of obstacles during his investigation. All of this suggests that a single person has been buying out shares in the club, but in a secretive and roundabout manner. According to the official paperwork, the money paid for the purchases have come from various off-shore accounts, which make the matter even more suspicious.

It is finally Mae who gives him the idea that someone must be trying to acquire a significant stake in the club and force Rebecca out eventually, which sounds like a villainous plan to take over Richmond. As Mae and Rupert, and then Rebecca as well, can think of only one person bullyish enough to try and do something like this, they believe that Rebecca’s treacherous ex-husband, Rupert Mannion, must be back to harass them. Although the characters do not suspect anyone else as of now, it seems increasingly likely that Zelda Southport might be mixed up with whoever the mysterious buyer is. Her eccentric and megalomaniac friend, Hugo Riddles, who is also a billionaire, might possibly be the one buying up all the shares, in hopes of taking over the football club.

Are Roy and Keeley finally back together?

Lastly, Ted Lasso season 4 episode 8 also deals with the situation between Roy and Keeley, who have both figured out by now that they love each other. But neither of them has acknowledged or expressed this to each other so far, and they instead keep bickering out of genuine, and some faked, disappointment in each other. Keeley wants Roy to attend the event organized at his old club, Chelsea FC, to commemorate his service to the team as a player and induct him into their wall of fame. Roy, on the other hand, hates any event or situation where he is praised or celebrated, and so he is frustrated at Keeley for having agreed to take him back to his old club. Ultimately, the two of them head to Chelsea together, first in Roy’s expensive car, which breaks down on the way, and then on the subway. It is during this journey that Roy reveals that he has broken up with Erin, and the emotions between the two are once again very palpable. Thus, by the time they reach the club, very late for the event, which has already wrapped up, Roy goes ahead and expresses his feelings to Keeley. She too admits that she has always feared seeing him with someone else, and their story finally comes full circle. Roy and Keeley finally kiss to confirm that they are back together once again, and with no intentions to leave each other this time around.
